correctness.rationale: The 54-vertex Gray incidence model has 27 points and 27 three-point axis lines; EOD splits independently into an exact point-on-each-line transversal (12 ternary affine Latin graphs of size nine) and nine-line grid tiling (21 choices). Distinct Latin slopes intersect in three points, giving minimum six-point replacements, so point trade graph is K_{3,3,3,3}. The 21 axis tilings consist of three 8-vertex cubes sharing their respective pure tilings; nearest line replacements are three. Their 36-edge glue graph T has eccentricity four and the full code-trade graph is Cartesian product with 252 vertices, 1566 edges, diameter/eccentricity six, and exact distance histogram (1566,4896,8460,9180,6444,1080). Symmetry group S3 wreath S3 of size 1296 splits line pure vs mixed configurations into orbits 36 and 216. No claim about arbitrary trades. The independent checker constructs all 12 codes and all 21 exact line tilings from scratch and recomputes distances.

evidence: Kuziak–Peterin–González Yero 2014 studies efficient open domination in graph products; the Gray graph is a girth-eight semisymmetric incidence graph rather than such a nontrivial graph product.
